public_rationale: In a transcript available on March 23, 2026, Huang declared that AGI had arrived, citing a hypothetical commercially successful application [e1]. That exchange does not demonstrate human-level breadth and resourcefulness [e1]. The September 2026 assessment describes GPT-6 Astra's reported capabilities and untested dimensions, finding the available evidence insufficient to establish AGI [e2]. Neither item establishes an independently verified AGI arrival that meets the early-resolution rule [e1] [e2].
limitations: “Soon” has no established endpoint. The end-of-2025 reference covers only part of the forecast.
The evidence does not comprehensively cover all systems through October 28, 2026.
Failure to establish AGI does not establish its absence or support the full forecast.

statement.excerpt: AGI (AI with the breadth and resourcesfulness of human intelligence) is not coming soon.
statement.document_title: Three years on, ChatGPT still isn't what it was cracked up to be – and it probably never will be

from_speaker: the breadth and resourcesfulness of human intelligence
certainly not at the end of this year
our_interpretation: The claim predicts that human-level general intelligence will not arrive in the near term after publication.
Soon does not identify a latest date. The explicit reference to the end of 2025 identifies an included subperiod, not the outer boundary of soon.
I therefore do not replace soon with an invented one-year or multi-year deadline.
A qualifying arrival clearly close to publication could contradict the claim. A borderline date would require resolving the timing ambiguity.
Human-level breadth and resourcefulness do not require flawless performance.
criteria.support_condition: Once a defensible endpoint for soon is established from the speaker's meaning, evidence shows that no qualifying AGI arrived within that interval. Continued absence without an endpoint cannot settle the full forecast.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A dated, independently validated system achieves human-level breadth and resourcefulness clearly within the near-term interval meant by the claim.

evidence.explanation: Huang explicitly claims AGI has arrived. The surrounding exchange concerns whether AI could create a commercially successful application; it does not demonstrate Marcus's broader human-intelligence criterion.

evidence.locator: Proposed tests of general intelligence, opening sentence
evidence.explanation: The assessment examines GPT-6 Astra's reported gains across proposed AGI tests and concludes that the published evidence is insufficient to establish AGI. It is an assessment of available evidence, not proof that AGI is absent or cannot arrive soon.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: An independently validated AGI achievement with human-level breadth and resourcefulness clearly within the intended near term would contradict the forecast. Support requires a defensible endpoint for “soon” and sufficient evidence that no qualifying AGI arrived within that interval.
